narrative: OMX30 faces a challenging open following the worst global equity session in months, with NASDAQ collapsing 5.52% and Asia-Pacific selling hard on AI/growth concerns. While the Swedish index maintains technical structure above its 200-MA (+2.6%), the weak ADX reading (8.6) and negative correlation bias (-2.995%) severely constrain upside momentum. A modest USD/SEK appreciation (+1.47%) supports large-cap exporters, but this is overwhelmed by risk-off contagion. The RSI at 47 offers no mean-reversion catalyst, and the lower Bollinger positioning suggests range-bound weakness. Expect OMX30 to test support near 3085–3100 unless US jobs data stabilizes sentiment.
morningBrief: OMX30 set for a soft open amid global tech rout and risk-off rotation. Watch support at 3100 (around yesterday's close of 3123); any breach could see 3085 (lower Bollinger band) as next target. Exporters (Volvo, Atlas Copco, Ericsson) may find some relief from USD/SEK at 9.87, but NASDAQ weakness (-5.52%) will weigh on tech sentiment and limit upside. Defensives (AstraZeneca, Essity, SEB) are the clear beneficiaries of flight-to-safety; banks may see NIM support from elevated yields but risk-off typically pressures loan demand. Industrials face input-cost headwinds from higher oil (Brent +0.29%). Key watch: US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET—any beat could stabilize sentiment and lift OMX30 from lows. VIX at 27.35 remains elevated; a move toward 30+ would trigger further selling.
